asserted.description: Asserted counts converted tasks naming a static desired state.

blocked.description: Blocked counts the placeholders a person must replace.

cannot_check.description: CannotCheck counts converted tasks that cannot run in check mode.

computed.description: Computed counts converted tasks whose desired state is decided at run time.

converted.description: Converted counts the tasks that converted, reviews included.

imperative.description: Imperative counts converted tasks with no desired state.

observe.description: Observe counts converted tasks that only read.

review.description: Review counts the converted tasks a person should read.

tasks.description: Tasks counts every task in the output.

Finding.description: Finding is one construct that did not convert cleanly, or converted in a way a person should know about. Every text field holds names and positions only, never a value from the playbook, so a report can be shared without leaking what the playbook held.

at.description: At is where the construct is in the playbook.

code.description: Code is the finding's stable machine code, from the closed set in codes.go, so an editor can attach one action per code.

emitted.description: Emitted is where the construct's task landed in the output, or nil (null in JSON) when it produced no task.

id.description: ID is this finding's name in this report ("F007"), which the emitted runbook's comment cites.

message.description: Message says what happened, in a sentence.

native.description: Native names the native construct to use instead, or what will add one, when there is something to say.

outcome.description: Outcome is what happened to the construct.

task.description: Task is the name of the task the construct belongs to, escaped for a terminal, or "" for a play-level construct.

Position.description: Position is a place in a file: the playbook a finding came from, or the runbook it landed in.

file.description: File is the file's name, relative to the playbook's directory for a playbook position and to the output directory for a runbook one.

Resolution.description: Resolution records a template resolved from the playbook itself: the variable, where its one definition is, and where it was used. Never the value.

defined_at.description: DefinedAt is where its one definition is.

used_at.description: UsedAt are the places a template read it.

RunbookResult.description: RunbookResult is one runbook the conversion wrote.

dag_version.description: DAGVersion is the built runbook's version, which a run reports.

file.description: File is the runbook's file name: <id>.yaml, or <id>.incomplete.yaml when a task in it is blocked.

hosts.description: Hosts is the runbook's hosts: one device name or tag, or "" when the plays named none a runbook can hold.

plays.description: Plays are the 1-based numbers of the plays the runbook holds.

runnable.description: Runnable is false when the runbook holds a blocked task, and so cannot run until a person resolves it.

TaskResult.description: TaskResult is one task the output holds: a converted task, or a placeholder for one that was not.

at.description: At is where the task is in the playbook.

can_check.description: CanCheck says whether the task can run in check mode; nil (null in JSON) for a blocked task, which was not asked.

check_reason.description: CheckReason says why a task cannot run in check mode.

class.description: Class is the task's state semantics, declared by the module table rather than inferred, or null for a blocked task.

class_basis.description: ClassBasis says in a phrase why the task has its class.

emitted.description: Emitted is where the task landed in the output runbook.

findings.description: Findings are the IDs of the findings the task cites.

fqcn.description: FQCN is the native method the task calls, or the unrunnable ansible.unconverted.<module> placeholder a blocked task becomes.

module.description: Module is the Ansible module the playbook task named.

name.description: Name is the task's name in the runbook, escaped for a terminal.

node_id.description: NodeID is the task's node in the built runbook, as a run reports it.

outcome.description: Outcome is converted, review or blocked.

param_keys.description: ParamKeys names the parameters the task passes, never their values.

runbook.description: Runbook is the id of the runbook the task landed in.

description: Report is everything the conversion found, as one model for the text view and --json alike.

cannot_check.description: CannotCheck lists the node IDs of converted tasks that cannot take part in check mode.

findings.description: Findings are the constructs that did not convert cleanly, each once.

playbook.description: Playbook is the converted playbook's file name, escaped for a terminal.

resolutions.description: Resolutions are the variables written into the runbooks from the playbook's own definitions.

runbooks.description: Runbooks are the runbooks the conversion wrote.

schema_version.description: SchemaVersion is this report's shape; it changes only when a field changes meaning or is removed.

tasks.description: Tasks are the tasks the runbooks hold, in order.
